processes.name: AllocatorProcess
processes.description:
Central resource allocator — reproduction of Karr 2012 hybrid partitioning. Runs first each tick: for each finite pool, available supply = pool level + this tick's metabolic production (_supply RATE in molecules/s times the timestep); partitions it among consumers' demands (demand__) by proportional allocation with a priority-weight hook, publishes grants (alloc__), and replenishes the pool by production. Supply and demand both scale with the timestep, so the partition is consistent at dt=1 s and at the coarse dt=300 s of the figure runs. Contract — per pool P: in

(level, float),

_supply (production RATE, molecules/s), demand__

(consumer->want, map). out

(replenish delta, float), alloc__

(consumer->grant, overwrite map). Fidelity: FAITHFUL to Karr's demand->allocate->run arbitration (proportional partition + priority hook).

processes.name: ChromosomeCondensationReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Chromosome condensation — reproduction of Karr 2012 ChromosomeCondensation.
SMC complexes bind DNA at ~smcSepNt spacing (KB 7130 nt) and compact it by loop formation; binding is limited by available SMC (and, in the original, ATP/water). Dynamics — saturating approach to full compaction driven by SMC binding:
    condensed_fraction += k · smc · (1 − condensed_fraction) · Δt   (clamped to [0,1]).
Contract — in: smc (available complexes). out: condensed_fraction (snapshot 0→1).
Fidelity: the SMC-limited saturating compaction is faithful. Compaction is carried as one genome-wide condensed fraction rather than per-site occupancy at smcSepNt spacing (7130 nt, via kb.karr_process_params('ChromosomeCondensation')); the SMC↔SMC-ADP ATPase cycle is delegated to the metabolite pools.

processes.name: ChromosomeDynamicsReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Chromosome DNA-protein interactions — coordinate-resolved reproduction of the dynamics behind Karr 2012 Fig 3.
The 580,070 bp chromosome is binned; RNA polymerases initiate at REAL per-gene start coordinates (KB-decoded, rRNA operon hotspot at its real ~170 kb locus) and elongate at ~50 nt/s; two replisomes initiate at oriC and advance OUTWARD, symmetrically, to terC (reported as signed positions ±off from oriC — a V, as in Fig 4D); the full DNA-binding-protein panel of Fig 4E occupies sites (SMC, SSB, GyrAB, Topo IV, DnaB, DnaN, DnaA, and the Fur/GntR/HrcA/LuxR transcription factors); and whenever a protein binds an already-occupied bin a binding×unbinding COLLISION is recorded by protein pair (RNA pol yields to the fork).
Contract — in: rna_polymerase (available RNA pols), replication_active (0/1), lesion_map (the SHARED per-site chromosome — damaged bins from DNADamage). out (snapshots): occupancy (bin→bound-time), fraction_explored, percent_rnap/dnap_explored, rna_pol_positions, dna_pol_positions, collisions (pair→count, incl. *||lesion stalls), n_collisions, dna_binding_density.
Fidelity: FAITHFUL gene coordinates (real KB per-gene loci + real rRNA operon position) and bidirectional oriC→terC fork geometry; the spatial approximation is the genome binning (n_bins), and structural-protein counts are representative. This process supplies the spatial layer the aspatial transcription/replication submodels lack, and reads the SHARED chromosome structure (gap #3): a DNA lesion on a polymerase's path stalls it (damage blocks elongation / the fork), so damage and the coordinate-resolved dynamics operate on ONE chromosome. Baseline damaging_agent=0 → no lesions → unchanged.

processes.name: ChromosomeSegregationReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Chromosome segregation — reproduction of Karr 2012 ChromosomeSegregation.
The original fires a single all-or-none segregation event once the chromosome is fully polymerized AND supercoiled (consuming GTP). Dynamics — gate on replication completion, then progress segregation to completion:
    if replicated_fraction ≥ complete_threshold: segregated_fraction += rate · Δt  (→1).
Contract — in: replicated_fraction (replication progress). out: segregated_fraction (snapshot 0→1).
Fidelity: the replication-completion gate driving segregation to completion is faithful. Segregation is a continuous ramp rather than the KB's discrete decatenation event; the per-event GTP cost (KB gtpCost 1.0, via kb.karr_process_params('ChromosomeSegregation')) is delegated to the metabolite pools.

processes.name: CytokinesisReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Cytokinesis — reproduction of Karr 2012 Cytokinesis (Li 2007 bind/bend/dissociate model).
The FtsZ-GTP Z-ring contracts by a cycle of filament binding, GTP-hydrolysis-driven bending, and dissociation; each cycle shrinks the pinched (septum) diameter. Once replication/segregation is complete (replicated_fraction ≥ threshold) and Z-ring filaments are present, the septum diameter shrinks from the M. genitalium cell width (~200 nm) toward 0 at a contraction rate scaled by ring availability; the cell divides when the diameter reaches 0.
The ORIGINAL whole-cell model terminates the simulation when the septum diameter reaches 0 — this is THE division trigger of the whole-cell model.
Contract — in (sensors): ftsz_ring_filaments, replicated_fraction. out: septum_diameter (nm snapshot), contraction_progress (0..1 snapshot), divided ∈ {0,1}.
Fidelity: the ring-gated, replication-gated pinch-to-division dynamics are faithful. The per-filament bind/bend/dissociate polygon-edge cycle (real KB constants rateFilamentBindingMembrane/Dissociation 0.7, rateFtsZGtpHydrolysis 0.15 /s, via kb.karr_process_params('Cytokinesis')) is lumped into one ring-availability-scaled nm/s contraction speed.

processes.name: DNADamageReproductionProcess
processes.description:
DNA damage — reproduction of Karr 2012 DNADamage.
The original selects damage sites with probability stepSize · rate · [radiation/agent] per reaction. Dynamics — one lumped Poisson lesion source (spontaneous baseline plus an agent-driven term):
    new_lesions ~ Poisson((base_rate + agent_rate · damaging_agent) · Δt).
Contract — in: damaging_agent (radiation/reactive-species level, default 0). out: lesions (additive Δ, new lesions this step).
Fidelity: the agent-driven Poisson damage law is faithful. Lesions are counted as one pool rather than typed and placed at vulnerable-motif sites; the per-reaction small-molecule reactant/product stoichiometry is delegated to the metabolite pools. Lesions are now tracked per-site on the shared chromosome structure (lesion_map) that damage adds to and repair clears from the same sites — the first consumer of the unified per-site chromosome (remaining DNA submodels staged). Constant provenance recorded in the gap-#5 audit (docs/CONSTANT_PROVENANCE.md).

processes.name: DNARepairReproductionProcess
processes.description:
DNA repair — reproduction of Karr 2012 DNARepair.
The original dispatches BER/NER/HR + polymerize + ligate subroutines over damaged sites, consuming ATP/dNTP. Dynamics — enzyme- and ATP-limited lesion clearance:
    present = n_lesions(lesion_map);
    repaired = min(present, rate · repair_enzyme · Δt, atp / atp_per_repair);
    lesion_map -= repaired sites (weighted-random selection);  Δlesions = −repaired;  Δatp = −repaired · atp_per_repair.
Contract — in: lesion_map (per-site counts, source of truth for repair demand), repair_enzyme (capacity), atp (energy cap). out: lesions (negative Δ), atp (negative Δ), lesion_map (negative per-site Δ).
Fidelity: the enzyme- and ATP-limited repair flux is faithful. The distinct BER/NER/HR pathways, DisA scanning, and per-base polymerize/ligate steps are lumped into one clearance flux; dNTP accounting is delegated to the metabolite pools. Consumption is arbitrated by the whole-cell resource allocator (Karr hybrid partitioning): capped each tick at its allocated ATP budget from the finite metabolism-replenished pool. Lesions are now tracked per-site on the shared chromosome structure (lesion_map) that damage adds to and repair clears from the same sites — the first consumer of the unified per-site chromosome (remaining DNA submodels staged).

processes.name: DNASupercoilingReproductionProcess
processes.description:
DNA supercoiling homeostasis — reproduction of Karr 2012 DNASupercoiling.
Gyrase introduces negative supercoils at its real KB activity rate (1.2 acts/gyrase/s, 2 ATP → 2 supercoils per act) while topoisomerases relax; the net effect drives the superhelical density σ toward the maintained negative setpoint (KB −0.06). Dynamics (first-order relaxation, gyrase- and ATP-limited):
    acts = min(gyrase·1.2·Δt, atp/2, supercoils_needed);  σ += sign(setpoint−σ)·acts/genome_turns;
    σ → setpoint;  Δatp = −2·acts.
Contract — in: gyrase (activity), atp (energy cap). out: superhelical_density (snapshot σ), atp (negative Δ).
Fidelity: FAITHFUL constants (real KB gyraseActivityRate 1.2, gyraseATPCost 2.0, setpoint −0.06, 10.5 bp/turn). σ is now tracked PER-REGION on the shared chromosome structure (linking_number: {region -> σ} over N_SUPERCOIL_REGIONS topological regions, the viva-native stand-in for CircularSparseMat's per-region linking numbers), and the genome-wide superhelical_density observable is their mean; gyrase acts are distributed across regions, each relaxed toward the setpoint. The advancing REPLICATION fork (read from the shared polymerized_map) overwinds the DNA just ahead of it, injecting positive supercoils into the fork-boundary regions — the source that makes the per-region linking numbers heterogeneous (gap #3). Gyrase maintains homeostasis: at the whole-cell timestep it relaxes the injection back within a tick, so σ stays ≈ setpoint everywhere with a small deviation at the fork region (the mean tracks the former single-pool σ; superhelical_density is unchanged as an observable). topoI/topoIV activity is lumped into the net gyrase relaxation (per-enzyme rates available via kb.karr_process_params('DNASupercoiling')). Consumption is arbitrated by the whole-cell resource allocator (Karr hybrid partitioning): capped each tick at its allocated ATP budget.

processes.name: FtsZPolymerizationReproductionProcess
processes.description:
FtsZ polymerization — reproduction of Karr 2012 FtsZPolymerization (Surovtsev 2008 kinetic scheme).
FtsZ is a CONSERVED pool partitioned between free subunits and the assembled Z-ring. GTP-driven activation moves FtsZ free→ring at k_on (real KB activationFwd 1.1 /s) and dissociation returns it ring→free at k_off (real KB activationRev 0.01 /s). The step is the exact closed-form two-state relaxation of the conserved pool over Δt:
    ring_eq = total · k_on/(k_on+k_off);  ring(t+Δt) = ring_eq + (ring−ring_eq)·e^(−(k_on+k_off)Δt),
costing 1 GTP per net new ring subunit and capping growth at available GTP. Because k_on ≫ k_off the ring reaches ≈ the full pool and drives the septum closed.
Contract — in (sensors): ftsz_monomer, gtp. out: ftsz_ring_filaments (Z-ring subunit count snapshot), gtp (negative delta, consumed).
Fidelity: FAITHFUL activation/dissociation constants (real KB activationFwd/Rev). The reduction is the assembly detail: a two-state free⇌ring relaxation stands in for the explicit nucleation/elongation/exchange mass-action multimers (their bimolecular fwd/rev constants are in different units and available via kb.karr_process_params('FtsZPolymerization')). Consumption is arbitrated by the whole-cell resource allocator (Karr hybrid partitioning): capped each tick at its allocated GTP budget from the finite metabolism-replenished pool.

processes.name: HostInteractionReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Host interaction — reproduction of Karr 2012 HostInteraction (qualitative, reporting).
The original decides adherence by a Boolean rule: adherent iff the terminal organelle is fully assembled AND all adhesin lipoproteins (MG_191/MgPa, MG_192, MG_217, MG_318) are present. Here that all-or-nothing AND is softened to a cooperative (Hill-like) saturating function of terminal_organelle_fraction, so adhesion rises steeply toward 1 only as assembly approaches completion.
Kept a Process (not a Step) because terminal_organelle_fraction is a genuine time-varying input, so adhesion_strength evolves over the cell cycle.
Contract — in (sensor): terminal_organelle_fraction (0..1). out: adhesion_strength (0..1 snapshot).
Fidelity: faithful to the original, which is itself qualitative/reporting-only; the Boolean adherence rule is rendered as a continuous cooperative function of assembly.

processes.name: MacromolecularComplexationReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Macromolecular Complexation — reproduction of Karr 2012 MacromolecularComplexation.
Monomers assemble into complexes limited by subunit availability. The default
stoichiometry is the REAL Karr knowledge base: all 161 protein-monomer-only
complexes with their true integer subunit counts (e.g. DNA_GYRASE = 2 MG_003 +
2 MG_004 = A₂B₂; MG_001_DIMER = 2 MG_001). Each complex forms up to its
limiting subunit,
    n_formed = floor(min over subunits(available / stoichiometry)),
processed in random order so shared subunits are drawn down as complexes compete
for the pool.
Contract — config: stoichiometry {complex: {monomer: n}} (default = real KB). in: monomers (map). out: monomers (neg Δ map), complexes (pos Δ map).
Fidelity: FAITHFUL stoichiometry (real KB subunit composition); the equilibration
is greedy limiting-subunit assembly per step rather than the MATLAB steady-state
network solve — the assembled amounts converge to the same subunit-limited counts.

processes.name: MassGrowthReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Cell mass & growth accounting — reproduction of Karr 2012 CellMass/CellGeometry.
Integrates the metabolism submodel's calibrated growth into total dry mass by exponential growth over each interval:
    Δmass = mass · (exp(μ · growth_fraction · Δt) − 1),   μ = ln2 / T_cycle
with T_cycle = 32400 s (≈ 9 h) the model's fitted cell-cycle length, so unperturbed growth (growth_fraction = 1) doubles the cell in ~9 h. Dry mass is partitioned into the fitted dry-weight fractions (protein 0.620, DNA 0.169, RNA 0.093, lipid 0.057, …); volume follows from wet mass and cell density. Division now fires when the EMERGENT macromolecule inventory (Σ species×MW) has doubled — the cell-cycle length is PREDICTED from the synthesis rates (phenotype from genotype), not imposed by the growth-law μ (which still sets the calibrated mass curve). Falls back to the 2×-birth growth-law trigger only until the emergent mass is populated (tick 0).
Contract — in: growth_fraction (unit-free growth from metabolism), mass (current dry fg). out: mass (additive Δ, fg), mass_fractions (per-component fg snapshot), volume (fL snapshot), division ∈ {0,1}.
Fidelity: FAITHFUL growth/composition phenotype — real fitted constants (dry-weight 3.93e-15 g, T_cycle 32400 s, component fractions, cell density). This is the calibrated growth-law form: mass follows metabolism-driven exponential growth partitioned by the fitted fractions, rather than being summed emergently from every species count × MW. In addition, the emergent macromolecular dry-mass composition (Σ species×MW over RNA/protein/DNA, from the real molecular inventory) is now computed and emitted (emergent_mass/emergent_mass_fractions) for validation against Karr's fitted fractions; the free-metabolite pool mass is emitted separately as a non-validated diagnostic (metabolite_mass), since current pool sizes are allocation-dynamics placeholders rather than calibrated copy numbers; the growth-law total above still drives division, pending synthesis calibration that would let the emergent total itself close the loop.

processes.name: MetabolismFbaReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Flux-balance-analysis metabolism — reproduction of the Karr 2012 Metabolism submodel.
Each 1 s step it maximizes the iPS189 biomass objective
    max cᵀv   s.t.   S·v = 0,   lb ≤ v ≤ ub
over the published Suthers 2009 M. genitalium reconstruction (351 reactions, 346 metabolites, 126 genes; solved with COBRA). Gene disruptions (Fig 6) knock out the disrupted genes' reactions; a kinetic-parameter change (Fig 7) scales a reaction's flux bound as a kcat/Vmax proxy. Both use a reverting model context so the cached network is never mutated.
Contract — in: nutrient_scale (carbon-uptake multiplier a sibling can throttle). out: growth_rate (biomass flux, raw iPS189 units), growth_fraction (growth_rate ÷ wild-type, the calibrated unit-free growth the mass submodel integrates), atp_production (ATP-synthase ATPS4r flux), gtp_production (summed GTP-linked kinase/transport flux: NDPK1/NDPK2 nucleoside-diphosphate kinases, GK1 guanylate kinase, GTPtp transport), feasible ∈ {0,1}; and the precursor SUPPLY rates atp/gtp/ntp/amino_acid_supply (molecules/s = base_supply·growth_fraction) that replenish the resource allocator's finite pools. GTP supply is the calibrated translation throttle (~2 GTP/peptide bond), fitted to Karr's ~70% protein dry-mass fraction; the raw FBA atp/gtp_production flux drives Fig 5 and is independent of these knobs.
Fidelity: FULL — the genuine published reconstruction the WCM's metabolism submodel was built on.
Reaction bounds can also be dynamically gated by the live proteome relative to a steady-state reference (enzyme_coupling) — the graded generalization of the discrete gene knockout above, scaling each gene-associated reaction's bound by its enzyme's current abundance over the reference instead of an all-or-nothing cut. ON by default (gap #6): the cell is seeded with a birth proteome and the reference is the emergent division proteome, so live/reference ≈ 0.5 at birth rising to ≈ 1 near division; a positive floor keeps reactions at basal activity under enzyme fluctuations. The absolute kcat·[enzyme] form awaits the KB kcats (gap #5).

processes.name: ParameterCalculatorReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Parameter calculator (ParCa) — reproduction of Karr 2012 FitConstants.
Computes the per-gene expression/decay/synthesis panel from the real observed knowledge-base data, fits it under the FitConstants linear constraints (RNA-mass balance, DnaA/FtsZ expression held, net-supercoiling zero), and closes the expression↔metabolism loop against the iPS189 FBA network.
Contract — in: none (reads the decoded knowledge-base datasets). out (snapshots): n_genes, median_mrna_synthesis_rate, mrna_halflife_min_mean, rrna_halflife_min, nmp_au_fraction, closed_loop_feasible, nmp_supply_flux, aa_supply_flux, growth_baseline.
Fidelity: genuine inputs (natively-decoded real KB data) + the FitConstants initialization and analytic QP + the metabolic-feasibility closure; the nonlinear metabolism resource coupling and heuristic refinement are the reduced part.

processes.name: ProteinActivationReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Protein Activation — reproduction of Karr 2012 ProteinActivation.
MATLAB's evaluateActivationRules partitions each regulatable protein between an active
and inactive form according to metabolite/stimulus rules. Here the active fraction of
each protein follows a Hill function of the regulator level:
    active_fraction = regulator^n / (K^n + regulator^n).
Contract — in: protein_counts (map), regulator (float). out: active_fraction (overwrite[map[float]], current per-protein value).
Fidelity: the equilibrium active/inactive partition is faithful; the KB's activation rules
are per-protein boolean/metabolite logic, approximated here by a shared Hill law driven by
one aggregate regulator level (the per-rule stimulus set is not carried on this panel).
Constant provenance recorded in the gap-#5 audit (docs/CONSTANT_PROVENANCE.md).

processes.name: ProteinDecayReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Stochastic protein decay — reproduction of Karr 2012 ProteinDecay.
Each protein degrades as a Poisson process at rate λ = ln2 / half-life over the full
~522-gene set:
    decayed_s ~ min(n_s, Poisson(n_s · λ_s · Δt))
balancing translation to set steady-state protein copy numbers.
Contract — in/out: protein_counts (per-gene protein; a negative-Δ map).
Fidelity: full gene set with species-level Poisson decay. The Karr KB carries no
per-monomer protein half-lives, so a single representative half-life is used (not a
fabricated per-gene KB value); protease/peptidase + ATP/amino-acid byproduct accounting
is delegated to the metabolite pools.

processes.name: ProteinFoldingReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Protein Folding — reproduction of Karr 2012 ProteinFolding.
Monomers in the 'notFolding' set relax spontaneously; the rest fold with chaperone
(GroEL/DnaK) assistance, which MATLAB drives as an ATP/enzyme-limited reaction Gillespie
loop. Here the folded fraction per step is
    frac = 1 - exp(-(spontaneous_rate + chaperone_rate·chaperone_count)·Δt),
the chaperone-assisted share = chaperone_rate·chaperone_count / total rate consumes ATP
(atp_per_fold ≈ 7 per GroEL cycle), and folds are capped at ATP availability.
Contract — in: unfolded (map), chaperone_count (float), atp (float). out: unfolded (neg map), folded (pos map), atp (neg Δ).
Fidelity: mechanism-faithful (spontaneous + chaperone-assisted, ATP-coupled). The Karr KB
carries no per-protein folding rate matrix, so spontaneous/chaperone rate constants are
order-of-magnitude physiological values, not fitted KB constants; prosthetic-group/ion
coordination is delegated to the metabolite pools. Consumption is arbitrated by the
whole-cell resource allocator (Karr hybrid partitioning): capped each tick at its allocated
ATP budget from the finite metabolism-replenished pool. Constant provenance recorded in
the gap-#5 audit (docs/CONSTANT_PROVENANCE.md).

processes.name: ProteinModificationReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Protein Modification — reproduction of Karr 2012 ProteinModification.
Ser/Thr/Tyr phosphorylation and lipoate/glutamate ligation of specific monomers.
MATLAB runs an enzyme+substrate-limited reaction Gillespie loop; here unmodified ->
modified at rate enzyme·specificRate·Δt, capped by ATP (~1 ATP per phosphoryl transfer).
Contract — in: unmodified (map), modification_enzyme (float), atp (float). out: unmodified (neg map), modified (pos map), atp (neg Δ).
Fidelity: mechanism-faithful (enzyme- and ATP-limited transfer). The Karr KB carries no
ProteinModification rate matrix, so the specific rate is an order-of-magnitude value;
the per-reaction cofactor stoichiometry is delegated to the metabolite pools. Consumption
is arbitrated by the whole-cell resource allocator (Karr hybrid partitioning): capped each
tick at its allocated ATP budget from the finite metabolism-replenished pool. Constant
provenance recorded in the gap-#5 audit (docs/CONSTANT_PROVENANCE.md).

processes.name: ProteinProcessingIIReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Protein Processing II — reproduction of Karr 2012 ProteinProcessingII.
After translocation, signal peptidase II (LspA/MG_210) cleaves the type-II signal
sequence for every translocated monomer; for the REAL KB lipoprotein subset
(lipoprotein_genes, per-protein signal-type classification decoded from the
knowledge base), diacylglyceryl transferase (Lgt/MG_086) additionally lipidates the
cysteine. MATLAB caps each transform at enzyme*specificRate*Δt shared proportionally:
    all translocated:  limit = signal_peptidase * 11.0 * Δt
    lipoprotein set:   additionally capped by diacylglyceryl_transferase * 0.0165 * Δt,
                       shared across just that subset.
Non-lipoproteins are limited only by the peptidase; the lipoprotein subset is further
throttled by the (much slower) Lgt step, so it clears more slowly but is never dropped —
un-transferred lipoprotein mass simply remains in 'translocated' for a later tick.
Contract — config: lipoprotein_genes (list[string], default = real KB lipoprotein
classification). in: translocated (map), signal_peptidase (LspA count, float), diacylglyceryl_transferase (Lgt count, float). out: translocated (neg map), processed_ii (pos map).
Fidelity: FAITHFUL peptidase kinetics (real KB rate 11.0 s⁻¹) AND the lipoprotein-specific
Lgt transfer (real KB rate 0.0165 s⁻¹), now applied as a per-protein throttle to the real
KB lipoprotein subset (14/~482 genes, decoded from the KB signal panel) rather than as a
global rate; PG160/byproducts are delegated to the metabolite pools.

processes.name: ProteinProcessingIReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Protein Processing I — reproduction of Karr 2012 ProteinProcessingI.
Peptide deformylase (MG_106) deformylates the N-terminal fMet of every nascent
monomer; methionine aminopeptidase (MG_172) additionally cleaves the N-terminal Met
for the REAL KB met-cleavage subset (per-protein classification decoded from the
knowledge base, met_cleavage_genes). MATLAB caps each transform at
enzyme*specificRate*Δt shared proportionally across waiting monomers:
    all nascent:      limit = deformylase*38.0*Δt
    met_cleavage set: additionally capped by aminopeptidase*6.0*Δt, shared across
                      just that subset.
Every monomer still advances nascent -> process_i_done each step; proteins outside
the met-cleavage set are deformylated and pass through without consuming
aminopeptidase capacity.
Contract — config: met_cleavage_genes (list[string], default = real KB met-cleavage
classification). in: nascent (per-gene, map), deformylase (MG_106 count, float), aminopeptidase (MG_172 count, float). out: nascent (Δ consumed, neg map), process_i_done (Δ produced, pos map).
Fidelity: FAITHFUL enzyme kinetics (real KB specific rates 38.0 / 6.0 s⁻¹) AND real
per-protein met-cleavage routing (35/~482 genes, decoded from the KB signal panel); water/formate/methionine byproducts delegated to the metabolite pools.

processes.name: ProteinTranslocationReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Protein Translocation — reproduction of Karr 2012 ProteinTranslocation.
Only the REAL KB secretory + lipoprotein subset (translocated_genes, per-protein
signal-type classification decoded from the knowledge base) is pushed through the
SecYEG pore by the SecA translocase, recognised via the GTP-driven signal recognition
particle. In the real KB the translocase specific rate (2.71e12 s⁻¹) is effectively
non-limiting, so the bottleneck is GTP through SRP recognition
(SRP_GTPUsedPerMonomer = 2.0, real KB):
    limit = min(translocase*2.71e12, gtp/2.0) * Δt,
applied only to the secretory/lipoprotein subset, consuming 2 GTP/monomer. Every OTHER
protein in process_i_done (cytoplasmic, no signal peptide) passes straight through to
translocated with no translocase/GTP gate, so the pipeline never stalls on
non-substrates.
Contract — config: translocated_genes (list[string], default = real KB
secretory+lipoprotein classification). in: process_i_done (map), translocase (float), gtp (float). out: process_i_done (neg map), translocated (pos map), gtp (neg Δ).
Fidelity: FAITHFUL rate constants (real KB translocase rate + SRP GTP/monomer = 2.0) AND
real per-protein substrate routing (20 secretory + 14 lipoprotein genes, decoded from the
KB signal panel); the ATP translocation-motor cost (35 aa/ATP) needs per-protein lengths
and is delegated to the metabolite pools. Consumption is arbitrated by the whole-cell
resource allocator (Karr hybrid partitioning): capped each tick at its allocated GTP
budget from the finite metabolism-replenished pool.

processes.name: RNAModificationReproductionProcess
processes.description:
RNA modification — reproduction of Karr 2012 RNAModification.
Modification enzymes formylate / lysidinate / methylate / pseudouridylate / thiolate
specific r/tRNA bases. Per species s:
    modified_s ~ min(n_s, Poisson(n_s · k_mod · Δt)),   sum_s modified_s ≤ enzyme · kcat · Δt
moving counts unmodified_rna → modified_rna, with the total capped by enzyme availability.
Mirrors evolveState's greedy loop that modifies unmodifiedRNAs → modifiedRNAs while enzyme
and substrate limits allow (reactionLimits gated on min over enzymes/substrates).
Contract — in: unmodified_rna (count map), modification_enzyme (available enzyme count). out: unmodified_rna (negative Δ), modified_rna (positive Δ).
Fidelity: mechanism-faithful (enzyme-budget-limited stochastic modification). The Karr KB
RNAModification parameter dict is empty, so k_mod / kcat are order-of-magnitude values (not
fabricated KB constants); one enzyme pool stands in for the 13 modification enzymes over 86
base modifications, and metabolite substrate/byproduct accounting is delegated to the pools.
Constant provenance recorded in the gap-#5 audit (docs/CONSTANT_PROVENANCE.md).

processes.name: RNAProcessingReproductionProcess
processes.description:
RNA processing — reproduction of Karr 2012 RNAProcessing.
Ribonucleases (RNase III/P/J, RsgA, DeaD) cleave nascent polycistronic r/t/tmRNA
transcripts into mature species. Per nascent species s:
    matured_s ~ min(n_s, Poisson(n_s · k_proc · Δt))
counts moving nascent_rna → mature_rna. Mirrors evolveState_Helper, which stochastically
matures unprocessedRNAs → processedRNAs up to enzyme/substrate limits. The pooled rate
k_proc is the mean of the REAL KB per-RNase specific rates (RNase III 7.7, P 6.0, J 0.37,
DeaD 1.48, RsgA 0.29 s⁻¹ → ~3.17 s⁻¹).
Contract — config: processing_rate (default = KB per-RNase mean), rnase_rates (the real
per-RNase map). in: nascent_rna (per-species count map). out: nascent_rna (negative Δ), mature_rna (positive Δ).
Fidelity: FAITHFUL rate constants (real KB per-RNase kcats). The lumping is species→RNase
assignment (one pooled first-order rate) — the panel does not carry which RNase cleaves
which transcript; cofactor (Mg²⁺/Zn²⁺) / ATP-GTP and intergenic-fragment accounting is
delegated to the metabolite pools.

processes.name: ReplicationInitiationReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Replication-initiation oriC assembly — reproduction of Karr 2012 ReplicationInitiation.
DnaA is activated to DnaA-ATP (ATP-gated) and recruited to the oriC R1–R5 boxes, polymerizing COOPERATIVELY: the per-step recruitment scales with (1 + complex/threshold), so the already-bound DnaA promotes further binding. Dynamics:
    recruited ~ min(dnaA_free, Poisson(k · (1 + complex/thr) · Δt))   [ATP>0 required]
    complex += recruited;  initiation_ready = 1 when complex ≥ threshold.
Contract — in: atp (activation gate), dnaA_free (recruitable monomers). out (snapshots): complex_size, initiation_ready (0/1).
Fidelity: the cooperative, ATP-gated, threshold-fired assembly is faithful. The oriC complex is tracked as one cooperative DnaA-ATP pool rather than the KB's five R1–R5 boxes with per-box binding/unbinding + DnaA-ADP reactivation (parameters available via kb.karr_process_params('ReplicationInitiation'); a single cooperativity factor stands in for the KB siteCooperativity 170 / stateCooperativity 2 constants).

processes.name: ReplicationReproductionProcess
processes.description:
dNTP-buffered three-phase replication — reproduction of the emergent cell-cycle regulation Karr 2012 uncovered (Fig 4).
INITIATION: DnaA accumulates stochastically (Poisson) into the oriC complex while dNTPs build up (at a reduced pre-S-phase rate) unconsumed; replication begins when DnaA ≥ threshold. REPLICATION: dNTP synthesis up-regulates to its full rate and DNA polymerase advances min(rate·Δt, dNTP) per step, consuming 1 dNTP/nt; done at terC after ~4 h (dNTP-synthesis-limited).
Because dNTPs accumulate during initiation, a longer initiation builds a larger surplus that makes replication FASTER — an emergent inverse initiation↔replication relationship that buffers total cell-cycle length (Fig 4C/D/E).
Contract — in: dntp_synthesis_scale (a sibling can couple metabolism→replication). out (snapshots): replicated_fraction, dntp_pool, dnaA_complex, phase_code (0=init,1=repl,2=done), chromosome_copy, initiation_duration, replication_duration, dntp_at_replication_start, and polymerized_map — the per-site polymerized-regions mask on the SHARED chromosome (bidirectional oriC→terC fork; gap #3), a spatial VIEW of replicated_fraction (Σ mask / n_bins == replicated_fraction, so unchanged).
Fidelity: FAITHFUL to the Fig 4 emergent regulation — the dNTP-buffered inverse initiation↔replication coupling and the real KB polymerase elongation rate (dnaPolymeraseElongationRate 100 nt/s ×2 replisomes) are reproduced. The reduction is the replisome mechanism: the lumped polymerase omits Okazaki-fragment/primer/ligase/SSB detail (real constants via kb.karr_process_params('Replication')).

processes.name: RibosomeAssemblyReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Ribosome Assembly — reproduction of Karr 2012 RibosomeAssembly.
30S/50S subunits assemble from ribosomal proteins + rRNA, requiring GTPase assembly
factors and GTP. Subunit composition is the REAL Karr KB: the 30S from its 20
r-protein monomers + 16S rRNA (MGrrnA16S), the 50S from its 32 r-protein monomers +
23S + 5S rRNA (MGrrnA23S, MGrrnA5S). MATLAB forms newComplexs = floor(min(gtp/
gtpPerComplex, water/.., RNAs, monomers)) gated on assembly enzymes; here each subunit
forms at
    n = floor(min(limiting r-protein, limiting rRNA, assembly_factor, gtp/gtp_per_complex))
consuming its subunits and GTP.
Contract — in: rprotein_counts (map), rrna_counts (map), assembly_factor (float), gtp (float). out: ribosome_30S (float Δ), ribosome_50S (float Δ), rprotein_counts (neg map), rrna_counts (neg map), gtp (neg Δ).
Fidelity: FAITHFUL subunit composition (full real r-protein + rRNA sets per subunit); water/GDP/Pi byproduct accounting omitted (tracked by the metabolite pools elsewhere). Consumption is arbitrated by the whole-cell resource allocator (Karr hybrid partitioning): capped each tick at its allocated GTP budget from the finite metabolism-replenished pool.

processes.name: RnaDecayReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Stochastic mRNA decay — reproduction of Karr 2012 RNADecay.
Each gene's mRNA degrades as a Poisson process at rate λ = ln2 / half-life, using the
REAL per-gene KB half-lives over the full ~522-gene set:
    decayed_s ~ min(n_s, Poisson(n_s · λ_s · Δt))
setting steady-state copy numbers together with transcription.
Contract — in/out: rna_counts (per-gene mRNA; a negative-Δ map).
Fidelity: FAITHFUL — real KB per-gene half-lives, full gene set; the NMP-salvage/water
byproduct accounting is delegated to the metabolite pools.

processes.name: TRNAAminoacylationReproductionProcess
processes.description:
tRNA aminoacylation — reproduction of Karr 2012 tRNAAminoacylation.
Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases conjugate amino acids to free tRNAs at a cost of 1 ATP each
(ATP -> AMP + PPi). The total number charged this step is
    N = floor( min( sum(free_tRNA), amino_acid, atp, synthetase · kcat · Δt ) )
distributed across species by multinomial draw proportional to free-tRNA counts, then
free_trna -> aminoacylated_trna and atp decremented by N. Mirrors evolveState's greedy
reactionLimits loop (min over synthetase/AA/ATP availability, weighted stochastic pick),
as one aggregate limit + multinomial partition.
Contract — in: free_trna (count map), amino_acid, atp, synthetase (pools/counts). out: free_trna (negative Δ), aminoacylated_trna (positive Δ), atp (negative Δ).
ORDERING: runs BEFORE Translation (charged tRNAs feed the ribosome same-tick).
Fidelity: mechanism-faithful (co-substrate-limited charging, ATP-coupled). The Karr KB
tRNAAminoacylation parameter dict is empty, so the synthetase kcat is an order-of-magnitude
value; one lumped synthetase pool + aggregate AA/ATP pools stand in for the 20 AA × 37
tRNA/tmRNA reactions with per-synthetase kcats and glutamyl/methionyl transferases.
Consumption is arbitrated by the whole-cell resource allocator (Karr hybrid partitioning):
capped each tick at its allocated ATP and amino_acid budgets from the finite
metabolism-replenished pools. Constant provenance recorded in the gap-#5 audit
(docs/CONSTANT_PROVENANCE.md).

processes.name: TerminalOrganelleAssemblyReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Terminal Organelle Assembly — reproduction of Karr 2012 TerminalOrganelleAssembly.
Adhesins/accessory proteins (HMW1/2/3, P1, P41, P24, P65) localize to the terminal
organelle in a fixed dependency ORDER: MATLAB only localizes a protein once its
prerequisite localization reactions pass a threshold. Here the assembled fraction is the
length of the leading run of ordered proteins present at/above threshold, divided by the
number of required proteins.
Contract — config: required order + threshold. in: adhesin_proteins (map). out: terminal_organelle_fraction (overwrite[float], current value 0..1).
Fidelity: the ordered-dependency assembly is faithful; the presence-at-threshold gate stands
in for the full per-reaction localization stoichiometry matrix (not carried on this panel).
Constant provenance recorded in the gap-#5 audit (docs/CONSTANT_PROVENANCE.md).

processes.name: TranscriptionReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Stochastic transcription — reproduction of Karr 2012 Transcription.
For every gene g in the full M. genitalium gene set (~522 genes), new mRNA per step is a
Poisson draw
    n_g ~ Poisson(k_g · (RNApol / RNApol_ref) · Δt)
capped by NTP supply (each transcript consumes length_g NTP; PPi released). Per-gene
rates k_g are ParCa-fitted from the real observed expression profile.
Contract — in: ntp (pool, molecules), rna_pol (available polymerase count). out: rna_counts (per-gene mRNA Δ, additive map), ntp (Δ consumed, negative).
Fidelity: FAITHFUL gene coverage (all ~522 genes) and ParCa-fitted per-gene rates. The
reduction is the RNA-polymerase state machine — initiation/elongation/termination are
collapsed into a single Poisson propensity scaled by available polymerase; reproduces the
bursty-mRNA behaviour of Fig 2G. Consumption is arbitrated by the whole-cell resource
allocator (Karr hybrid partitioning): capped each tick at its allocated NTP budget from the
finite metabolism-replenished pool.

processes.name: TranscriptionalRegulationReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Transcriptional regulation — reproduction of Karr 2012 TranscriptionalRegulation.
TFs bind accessible promoter sites and multiply each transcription unit's RNA-pol binding
probability by a fold change. Per gene g:
    fold_change_g = prod over regulating TF f of  (fc_{f,g} ** activity_f)
mirroring calcBindingProbabilityFoldChange (foldChange = prod of tfActivities;
otherFoldChanges = prod(otherActivities .^ (enzymes>0))). An activity of 0 leaves the gene
unregulated (fold change 1); an activated TF pushes fc_{f,g}>1, a repressor fc_{f,g}<1.
The default network is the REAL KB regulatory network: 52 genes regulated by the 5 genuine
M. genitalium TFs (MG_127/MG_236/MG_101 monomers, MG_205/MG_428 dimers) with the true
per-edge fold-changes decoded from the TranscriptionUnit objects.
Contract — config: gene_regulation (default = real KB network). in: tf_activity (per-TF fractional activity map). out: fold_change (per-gene multiplicative fold change, an overwrite sensor map).
Fidelity: FAITHFUL regulatory network (real KB TF→gene edges + real fold-changes). The
reduction is the promoter-occupancy / chromosome-accessibility state machine, collapsed to
the fold-change law above driven by continuous TF activity.

processes.name: TranslationReproductionProcess
processes.description:
Stochastic translation — reproduction of Karr 2012 Translation.
For every gene g in the full M. genitalium gene set (~522 genes), new protein per step is
Poisson in the current mRNA copy number
    n_g ~ Poisson(r_g · mRNA_g · Δt)
capped by GTP supply. Each chain of gene g costs gtp_per_peptide_bond · (length_g/3)
GTP (~2 GTP per peptide bond over the peptide's residues), so a long protein draws
proportionally more of the shared GTP budget than a short one. Per-gene rates r_g are
ParCa-fitted.
Contract — in: rna_counts (per-gene mRNA copies), gtp (pool, molecules). out: protein_counts (per-gene protein Δ, additive map), gtp (Δ consumed, negative).
Fidelity: FAITHFUL gene coverage (all ~522 genes) and ParCa-fitted per-gene rates. The
reduction is the ribosome state machine (elongation/tmRNA stalling collapsed into one
mRNA-proportional, GTP-limited propensity); drives the Fig 2G/2H mRNA↔protein decoupling
and the translation share of the Fig 5 energy budget. Consumption is arbitrated by the
whole-cell resource allocator (Karr hybrid partitioning): capped each tick at its allocated
GTP budget from the finite metabolism-replenished pool.

processes.name: Analysis
processes.description:
Live-``conn`` analysis base: reads sim output via a DuckDB connection +
the ParCa ``sim_data``, and emits a rendered ``view`` (HTML) plus optional
``data`` (map). Faithful native ports of vEcoli's ``plot()`` analyses build
on this base (cf. the record-based ``AnalysisStep`` for emitted-observable
analyses). Subclasses set ``scale`` + ``name`` and implement ``analyze``.

Live, non-serializable handles (``conn``, ``sim_data``) are injected by the
runner into the state dict passed to ``update``; ``inputs()`` declares them
for discoverability with a permissive ("any") type.

Genuinely distinct from ``AnalysisStep`` (its parent only for the shared
``scale``/registry machinery via ``__init_subclass__``) — this is NOT a
thin alias. v2ecoli's production ``analysis_runner.py::run_analyses()``
drives ~30 concrete subclasses through exactly this surface (calling
``update()`` with ``conn``/``history_sql``/``sim_data``/... injected
directly into ``state``, bypassing ``ResultsHandle`` entirely), so
``update()`` here must read those keys straight off ``state`` — it must
NOT read a ``ResultsHandle`` from ``state["results"]`` the way
``AnalysisStep.update()`` does. (A prior collapse of this base into
``AnalysisStep`` silently dropped the injected conn/history_sql/sim_data
kwargs, breaking all ~30 subclasses; restored here to the original
pre-collapse behavior.)

processes.name: AnalysisStep
processes.description:
Canonical base for post-sim analyses.

Reads the ``ResultsHandle`` that ``ResultsStep`` wrote to the ``results``
store and implements ``analyze(rows) -> dict`` over
``results.records(scale=self.scale)``. Subclasses that need direct SQL
access instead of record dicts can pull ``results.conn()`` (lazy DuckDB)
or ``results.sim_data`` from within ``analyze`` (the handle is available
via the ``results`` input if a subclass overrides ``update`` to keep it).
Subclasses set ``scale`` (one of ``ANALYSIS_SCALES``) + ``name``.

``Analysis`` (below) is a *separate*, genuinely distinct base for the
live-``conn`` surface v2ecoli's ``analysis_runner.py`` drives directly —
it only shares ``__init_subclass__``'s ``scale``/registry machinery with
this class, not ``update()``/``inputs()``/``outputs()``. (An earlier
revision collapsed ``Analysis`` into a thin alias of this class, which
silently dropped the injected ``conn``/``history_sql``/``sim_data``
kwargs and broke every v2ecoli ``Analysis`` subclass; do not repeat
that — the two bases stay distinct.) For backward compatibility,
``update()`` here also accepts a plain list in the ``results`` store
(the pre-``ResultsHandle`` contract) — used as-is, no handle required.

processes.name: ConsoleEmitter
processes.description: Print state to console each timestep.

processes.name: Distribution
processes.description:
Histogram of an observable's distribution.

Inputs (declared types):
  samples: list[float] — the values to bin

processes.name: Heatmap
processes.description:
Color matrix over a 2D parameter sweep.

Inputs (declared types):
  x_params: list[float]
  y_params: list[float]
  z_values: list[list[float]]  — z[y_idx][x_idx]

processes.name: InvestigationAnalysisStep
processes.description:
One investigation-level Analysis (e.g. ``comparison_matrix``), wired to
every study whose verdict it needs. ``inputs()`` — one ``"node"`` port per
``study_slugs`` entry, wired by the generator to that study's
``StudyStep`` ``result`` store — both orders this step to run AFTER those
studies (the engine's ``determine_steps`` dependency ordering, same
mechanism as ``StudyStep``'s ``prereq_*`` ports) AND delivers each study's
result dict (which carries its ``verdict``) as this step's wired state.

``update()`` assembles ``config_verdicts = {slug: verdict}`` from the wired
study results via ``_extract_study_verdict`` — each ``config_verdicts[slug]``
is the actual verdict dict (``res["analyses"][verdict_analysis]["verdict"]``,
falling back to ``res["verdict"]``, falling back to the raw result), not the
raw ``run_study`` reply. Merges the result into the static ``params``, and
dispatches to the ``run_investigation_analysis`` worker capability (design:
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-01-investigation-as-composite-design.md,
§Architecture 2-3; refined by
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-store-dataflow-refactor-design.md §2).
Bypasses the parquet-coupled ``run_study_analyses`` path entirely — the
#712 blocker this exists to route around.

NAME: keep this ``InvestigationAnalysisStep``, NOT ``AnalysisStep`` — the
latter collides with ``v2ecoli.workflow.analysis.AnalysisStep`` for the
short link-registry alias in a v2ecoli venv, so ``local:AnalysisStep`` would
silently resolve to the wrong class. The unique name lets the generator use
the plain ``local:InvestigationAnalysisStep`` address safely.

processes.name: JSONEmitter
processes.description:
Append simulation state to a persistent JSON Lines file each timestep.

Each recorded tick is one JSON object on its own line (``.json`` file in
JSON Lines / ``jsonl`` form). This is an append-only O(1)-per-tick write:
the previous behaviour re-read and re-serialized the entire history on
every tick (O(n) per tick -> O(n^2) per run), which dominated long runs.

``query`` transparently reads BOTH the current line-delimited format and
the legacy single JSON-array format, so files written by older versions
remain readable.

processes.name: ParamVsObservable
processes.description:
Plot reduced observable values across a sweep.

Inputs (declared types):
  sweep_param_values: list[float] — x-axis (one value per run in the sweep)
  reduced_observable: list[float] — y-axis (reduced trajectory per run)

processes.name: PhaseSpace
processes.description:
XY trajectory of two observables.

Inputs (declared types):
  x: list[float]
  y: list[float]

processes.name: RAMEmitter
processes.description:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).

processes.name: ResultsStep
processes.description:
The head of the post-sim Step family: reads a finished run's emitted
results location (store path(s), and optionally a sim_data reference)
from config or from a wired-in state input, and writes one
``ResultsHandle`` to the ``results`` store. Every downstream Step —
``AnalysisStep``, ``ReportCardStep``, etc. — reads from that single
handle, so a composite shaped ``[emitter output] -> ResultsStep ->
{AnalysisStep, ReportCardStep, ...}`` gives every post-sim Step the same
view of the run, computed once (``ResultsHandle`` caches its own
``.records()``/``.conn()``, so fan-out doesn't re-read the store).

Config keys (all optional): ``paths`` (list[str]), ``sim_data_ref``
(any), ``simulation_id`` (str). A same-named, non-empty ``state`` input
overrides the matching config key, so a composite can wire an upstream
store (e.g. a run-finished notification carrying the real output path)
instead of hard-coding a path in config.

processes.name: StudyStep
processes.description:
Step base class.

A `Step` is a stateless, non-temporal computational unit within a composite process.
It is triggered when its data dependencies are satisfied, functioning like a reaction
or transformation rule.

Override the `.update()` method to define custom behavior.

Override `.triggers()` to control which input ports trigger the step.
By default all inputs trigger — the step runs whenever any input changes.
To make some inputs "silent" (received but not triggering), return only
the triggering subset from `triggers()`.

Class attributes for memoization:
    ``_cache`` — ``'none'`` (default) or ``'by_hash'``. When
        ``'by_hash'``, ``invoke()`` hashes the Step's config and the
        incoming state, keys a class-level cache by
        ``(schema_version, hash)``, and reuses prior outputs on a
        hit. Requires ``_schema_version``.
    ``_schema_version`` — opaque string identifying the Step's
        output-relevant implementation version. Bumping invalidates
        all prior cache entries under the old version. Required when
        ``_cache == 'by_hash'``.

processes.name: TestReportStep
processes.description:
Evaluate-tail Step: aggregate the run's TestStep verdicts into
report.json and diff against the previous run (diff.json). Emits
``{report, diff, gate}``. ``run_id`` is never generated internally — it
arrives via config/state (workflow-engine ``Date.now()``-free rule).

processes.name: TestStep
processes.description:
A test (formerly "report card") as a visualization-like Step (sibling of
``Analysis`` and ``VisualizationStep``): emits ``view`` (HTML) + ``data``
(verdict map). Unlike ``Analysis`` — which consumes a live DuckDB sim-output
connection — a test's input is a ``StudyContext`` (the study's spec + dir),
so tests grade run-free. Subclasses set ``name`` and implement
``applies(study)`` + ``build(study) -> (verdict_dict, html) | None``. A named
subclass auto-registers in ``TEST_REGISTRY`` and, kind-tagged, in
``POST_SIM_REGISTRY``.

Gating convention: a test's verdict dict is free-form (existing tests are
not required to change), but a test intended to gate a study's Evaluate
stage should shape its verdict as ``{"status": "pass"|"fail"|"warn",
"checks": [...], "summary": <str>}`` so a generic gate can read
``data["status"]`` without knowing the test. ``checks`` is a list of
per-check detail dicts (test-defined shape); ``summary`` is a short
human-readable readout of the verdict.

processes.name: TimeSeriesFromObservables
processes.description:
Multi-observable time series, self-contained.

Config keys (user-set in ``study.yaml.visualizations[].config``):

  - ``observables: list[str]`` (required) — observable names to plot.
    Matched against ``study.yaml.observables[].name`` for units
    + against the ``observables`` map in runs.db ``history.state``
    for data.
  - ``title: str`` (optional) — chart title. Defaults to ``""``.
  - ``sources: list[str]`` (optional) — restrict to runs whose
    ``sim_name`` is in this list. Default: all runs.

Config keys injected by the renderer (private; users don't set
these):

  - ``_runs_db_path: str`` — absolute path to the study's runs.db.
    When absent, the chart renders an empty-data placeholder.
  - ``_study_yaml_path: str`` — absolute path to study.yaml. Used
    to look up per-observable ``units``. When absent, units are
    omitted from axis labels.

Inputs: none (the class plumbs its own data). The renderer's
``build_viz_composite`` skips inputs_map plumbing when a viz class
declares no inputs.

processes.name: TimeSeriesPlot
processes.description:
Plot one or more observables vs time.

Inputs (declared types):
  observable: list[float]   — trajectory values, or list-of-lists for multi-run
  time:       list[float]   — same shape as observable

processes.name: VisualizationStep
processes.description:
A post-sim visualization Step: emits a rendered ``view`` (HTML) + ``data``
(map), like ``Analysis`` but tagged ``kind="visualization"`` so the flush can
route it distinctly. Subclasses set ``name`` and implement
``render(study) -> (html, data) | None``. Inputs default to a StudyContext;
override ``inputs()`` to consume the run extraction instead.

processes.name: _StudyGateCard
processes.description:
Minimal gating report card over a ``CompositeTask``'s per-seed results.

Grades the composite's own execution state -- whether every scattered
seed actually produced a result -- rather than reading emitted
observables off a real ``ResultsHandle``. That ResultsStep/parquet
integration is already proven elsewhere (``viva_superpowers.ResultsStep``
+ the v2ecoli milestone workflow); this minimal slice's gate grades
run-free off what the study DAG itself already knows, keeping the toy
slice runnable with no emitter/parquet machinery at all. Verdict shape
follows the gating convention: ``{status, checks, summary}`` with
``status`` in ``{"pass", "fail"}`` (``"warn"`` is a valid status in the
wider vocabulary this compiles toward -- e.g. a future card grading
partial seed coverage -- just not one this minimal gate emits itself).

processes.name: edge
processes.description:
Base class for all computational edges in the bigraph schema.

Edges define the interface between simulation processes and the global state,
specifying the structure of input and output ports using bigraph types
(e.g., 'float', 'map[float]', 'list[integer]', etc.).

Upon instantiation, each edge registers its port types with the core.

processes.name: Clock
processes.description:
Emit an integer ``tick`` step counter each update.

(For absolute simulation time, read the engine-maintained ``global_time``
store directly — see the module docstring.)

processes.name: Intervention
processes.description: Apply a specific perturbation to one target store (see module docstring).

processes.name: MathExpressionStep
processes.description:
Evaluate a set of user-configured mathematical expressions as a single Step.

Configuration
-------------
expressions : list[dict]
    List of ``{"out": <str>, "expr": <str>}`` entries. Each ``out`` becomes
    an output port and state field.
params : dict[str, float], optional
    Named constants available to expressions without becoming input ports.
functions : str, optional
    SymPy ``lambdify`` backend module name (default ``"numpy"``).
debug : bool, optional
    If True, prints inferred ports, dependency order, and compilation details.

Notes
-----
Single-pass evaluation in dependency order; not a simultaneous-equation
solver. Cyclic dependencies require a different approach (fixed-point
iteration or root finding).

processes.name: SQLiteEmitter
processes.description:
Append simulation state to a SQLite database each timestep.

One row per step, with the full state tree stored as JSON. The database
file is a single ``.db`` file that can be opened with any SQLite client,
queried with SQL, and kept for long-term storage. Multiple simulations
can share one file — rows are partitioned by ``simulation_id``.

To record the composite config or other metadata alongside the history
rows, call :func:`save_simulation_metadata` after constructing the
Composite — the emitter itself only writes the per-step history rows.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 = every
tick). The ``step`` column still stores the true composite tick number,
so time-series produced from the history reflect the real cadence even
though intermediate ticks were not persisted. Use this when a Composite
fires the emitter very often (small intervals, long runs) and you don't
need every tick in the archive — it's the cheapest way to shrink the
write volume without losing the simulation's time axis.

``batch_size`` buffers up to N recorded rows in memory and flushes them
in a single SQL transaction (default 1 = write each row immediately).
With ``batch_size=100`` the per-row fsync overhead is amortized across
the batch, giving a large speedup on high-frequency runs. Unflushed
rows are guaranteed to be written on ``close()`` and on the next
``query()``; a hard crash before flush loses the buffered rows.

imports.name: pbg_parsimony
imports.description:
cellPACK-style 3D packing engine (Ingredient/Capsule/Chromosome/
build_pack) used by viva_mgen.structural to pack the whole-cell
molecular roster into a single-membrane M. genitalium capsule.
